Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] thanks for your patience. 

In FR we do commit to reverse on Wednesdays the money generated during the week before. Whilst T&Cs foresee the case where the payment is delayed for some issues on the passenger’s side ( please see below article 6.5 FR T&Cs corresponding to 6.6 of Global drivers T&Cs), they stay silent on delays / cancellation due to driver’s fraud  or attempt to fraud.

_6.5. We are not obliged to pay you the Fare due from the Passenger if the In-app Payment failed because Passenger’s credit card or other payment is cancelled or is unsuccessful for other reasons. In such case we will help you in requesting the Fare due from the Passenger and shall transmit it to you once the Passenger has made the requested payment._



Ideally we should amend the T&Cs before rolling out the feature. However, changes will be minor and I wonder what are the volumes so far of delayed/cancelled payments due to fraud in FR, before launching the heavy process of amending T&Cs and serving 14 day- prior notice before entry into force of the amendments. Do you have any visibility on this? I guess the risk to go live without amending T&Cs is potentially increasing prelitigation ( and litigation ) cases where drivers claim for the money, but perhaps we can live with it till the next round of broader review of T&Cs, specially if volume forecast is low.

Communications drafts are ok and would perfectly work for FR! 

Thanks, 

Michela

We cannot proceed with this ticket because of the below reasons.

* Before removing the identification blocks. We need to have the identification checks for the London. But currently the London identification checks are missing ([@divyansh.kumar|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02CCN2T2GZ] would better explain London checks scenario in details)
* {{/internal/driver/endCurrentIdentificationBlocks}} endpoint currently cancels all the active blocks in a transaction. Which means that if one of the block id fails then the entire transaction is rolled back.
* But calling {{/cancelBlockById}} one by one would leave the system the in partial state if the one of them fails. Instead, {{/cancelBlockById}} api can take list of block ids and cancel them in a transaction. In this way we make sure that system is not in partial state.
* {{endCurrentIdentificationBlocks}} behaves slightly differently than how {{endScheduledBlock}}  behaves (called by {{cancelBlockById}} ). 
** The {{endScheduledBlock}} so far was triggered only from admin and does not cancel a block if the UK driver has a selected car. Currently there is no prerequisite check happening for {{/internal/driver/endCurrentIdentificationBlocks}} api. 
** But with  {{/cancelBlockById}}  there is a prerequisite check, see [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/061759e8ee8cc2a078740d2570e7a3715f097be6/src/rides/driver/fleet/main/driver/service/DriverScheduledBlockingService.ts#L176].

Hence before moving forward we will need to discuss the above 
cc  [@divyansh.kumar|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02CCN2T2GZ]

Hey [~accountid:61b0698dfe9f3000680f0585] 

*1. Legal Framework (regarding verifying driving license)* 
- *Obligation to check the driving license* _(Road Traffic Act)_*:* 
As a provider of a car sharing service, we have a right/obligation to check whether a user is in possession of a valid driving licence. This right is derived from § 21 (1) no. 2 StVG (Straßenverkehrsgesetz)

_“(1) A sentence not exceeding one year or a monetary penalty shall be imposed on anyone who (...)_
_2. as the “keeper” (Halter) of a motor vehicle orders or allows someone to drive the vehicle who does not have the required driving licence (...).”_

- *German Federal Data Protection Law (BDSG - in English:* [https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_bdsg/index.html|https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_bdsg/index.html|smart-link] *):*
The opening clauses (GDPR) are implemented in a uniform Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG). I have not found any explicit rules for the processing of identity documents _(Attention: Part 3 of the Act (§§ 45 ff. ) is the implementation of Directive (EU) 2016/680 and therefore only applies to the processing of personal data by public bodies responsible for the prevention, investigation, detection, prosecution or punishment of criminal offences or misdemeanours.)_

In connection with the collection, processing and storage of driving licence data, I was not able to find literature/legislation on car sharing. However, since Germany is also the country where a company car is a matter of good manners, there is some information on the processing of driving licence data. 

*The legal basis for a driving licence check by the owner of the vehicle is, in the broadest sense, the Road Traffic Act. The owner of the vehicle has the right to protect himself by appropriate means against the consequences of infringements and damage (see the obligation to check driving licences mentioned above). The driving licence check regularly involves personal data. The regulations of the GDPR apply accordingly to the collection, processing and storage.* 

- *No legal prohibition regarding driving licence-copies.*
In contrast to copies of identity cards, I could not find any concrete legal restrictions (To make a copy of the identity card is only permissible with the consent of the card holder (§ 20 paragraph 2 PAuswG). The provision also requires that the copy of the ID card must be clearly and permanently recognisable as a copy.

*2. Data Protection Authorities (Storage of driving license data)*
It is disputed whether the obligation to check also provides a legal basis for making copies of driving licences. Looking at the views of the individual authorities, there is no unified opinion in connection with the storage of driving licence data (of employees). *(High possibility that Authorities would deny it).*

* The view of the *Bremen authority (*[*38th Annual Report of the State Commissioner for Data Protection, 2015, point 11.2*|https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=&ved=2ahUKEwi5lIKXguD9AhXsCRAIHSlmCeYQFnoECA0QAQ&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datenschutz.bremen.de%2Fsixcms%2Fmedia.php%2F13%2F38%2520Jahresbericht%2520Datenschutz.pdf&usg=AOvVaw2Dhm2g1J-iXkQODPGbs_EC]*)* is the strictest.

The annual report states: _"We do not consider it necessary to make copies of driving licences. It is sufficient to ascertain at each check whether the employee has a valid driving licence. Moreover, making copies of driving licences constitutes double storage, which violates the legal principle of data economy."_

* In *Hessen*, the case is seen in a slightly more differentiated way ([*44th Activity Report of the Hessian Data Protection Commissioner, 2015, point 4.5.2*|https://datenschutz.hessen.de/sites/datenschutz.hessen.de/files/2022-08/2015_44_tb_0.pdf]):

_"The production of copies of driving licences and their filing in the personnel files may also be necessary under special circumstances."_

If there are "special circumstances", a copy of the driving licence should therefore be necessary and thus lawful. Problem: When do these "special circumstances" exist? Ultimately, as with "necessity", this is also an undefined (legal) concept that does not entail legal certainty. The opinion from Hessen, however, softens the prohibition and at least shows that constellations are certainly possible in which copies of driving licences may be made.

* The responsible *Bavarian authority* is unusually magnanimous [*(6th Activity Report of the Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision for the years 2013 and 2014, point 15.5)*|https://www.lda.bayern.de/media/baylda_report_06.pdf]:

_"Since, moreover, the driving licence is only likely to contain data which are already known to the employer anyway or which are rather trivial (e.g. driving licence class), we consider it justifiable for the employer to copy the driving licence."_

*In my opinion, it would not be possible to derive a legal obligation (within the meaning of Art 6 (1) (c) of the GDPR) to make copies of driving licences directly from the Road Traffic Act.*

Hello, from tax side we are good if we consider these collected fees as donations and reflect these in our accounting as only balance sheet transactions. 

Then we would just act as collector and forwarder of the donations with no tax impact:

* there would be no VAT added on the fee;
* there would be no corporate income tax payable on the donation. 

But there are some general considerations that we have seen in similar cases - for clarity, we would not advise calling it a booking fee since there is already a big mess around this term and we use the booking fees for too many different things.

Also a note from the Commerce Compliance team (Gerly Lõhmus) - _Any fees applied towards passengers which are contractually charged by Bolt require FinReg sign-off. Those cannot be named a "booking fee":_ [_https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QyNGrGKNah6A5HcFGBdLdPZgluJaqPenkuHvOpGOf8w/edit#slide=id.g13f9179890d_0_535_|https://www.google.com/url?q=https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QyNGrGKNah6A5HcFGBdLdPZgluJaqPenkuHvOpGOf8w/edit%23slide%3Did.g13f9179890d_0_535&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1678975022146050&usg=AOvVaw0gdYJlEbZq1sQS_N5h00C9]

Sometimes Prometheus fails to scrape the data for a service due to various reasons (network issues, service is unavailable, etc.). This results in a metric loss for a short period of time (check the screenshot of how it looks). Our criti’s query evaluates 2 instant vectors - “now” and “N sec offset from now”. Query results with a value if the first vector value is different from the second. Knowing that our metric is a counter, a different result will be in case of an increase OR in case of a reset (reset will not result as {{unless}} operator ignores it). But what will happen if the offset vector points to the empty metric? The query sees it as a 0 and responds with a non-zero value (which triggers a false-positive).
The solution is to take the maximum value for both vectors for a period. This would ignore such “metric holes” as usually, we loose only about 15-30 seconds of data (1-2 scraping intervals).

New query:

{noformat}sum by (node_service_id, node_shard_id, tag) (max_over_time(nodejs:logger:messages_by_level_total{level="critical"}[@@TS@@]) unless max_over_time(nodejs:logger:messages_by_level_total{level="critical"}[@@TS@@] offset @@TS@@)){noformat}

*Summary:* 
Taking into account the EDPB guidelines, I do not consider the storage of the driving licence-copy to be necessary for the fulfilment of the contract, as the provision of the service can also be achieved by other less intrusive means. However, there is a clear legal obligation to verify the driving licence, which, in my opinion, cannot be extended to the storage of the copy without further ado, as there are other means for the proper documentation of the verification. 

For any storage in connection with automated verification data (which is probably based on the processing of biometric data), explicit consent (Art 9(2)(a)) and, depending on the risk of litigation, storage for the defence of legal claims (Art 9(2)(f)) would be appropriate. 

*Remarks:* 

*A. Legal Basis for keeping driving license copies*
According to current German law, German driving licences must be reissued at regular intervals (15 years). This is purely an administrative matter - the right to drive itself remains unchanged. Additional medical examinations or other tests such as a repetition of the driving test are not associated with this.

* All new driving licence documents issued after 19.1.2013 have an expiry date. They are limited to 15 years. The time limit serves as a security against expiry. A new document is issued without an examination and without a health check.
* All driving licences issued before 19.1.2013 must be exchanged by 19.1.2033 at the latest. There is a time schedule with 2 tables for the exchange. The date of issue of the driving licence document and not the date of acquisition of the driving licence class is decisive for the question of when the specific driving licence document must be exchanged.

In my view, this complicates the argument that the storage of a driving licence-copy is necessary for the performance of the contract. If you take Art 6(1)(b) into account, the processing (in this case the storage) must be necessary for the performance of the contract. The concept of "necessary for the performance of a contract" is not just about what is allowed under the clauses of a contract or what is in the contract clauses. The concept of necessity has an independent meaning in Union law, which must reflect the objectives of data protection law.

In this context, the EDPB states the guidelines still adopted by the Article 29 Working Party on the corresponding provision of the previous Directive, according to which 'necessary for the performance of a contract with the data subject' applies:
_”... must be interpreted strictly and does not cover situations where the processing is not genuinely necessary for the performance of a contract, but rather unilaterally imposed on the data subject by the controller. Also the fact that some processing is covered by a contract does not automatically mean that the processing is necessary for its performance. [...] Even if these processing activities are specifically mentioned in the small print of the contract, this fact alone does not make them ‘necessary’ for the performance of the contract.” (Article 29 Working Party Opinion 06/2014 on the notion of legitimate interests of the data controller under Article 7 of Directive 95/46/EC (WP217), page 16–17.)_

The EDPB also points to the following passage in these Article 29 Working Party Guidelines, which states:
_”There is a clear connection here between the assessment of necessity and compliance with the purpose limitation principle. It is important to determine the exact rationale of the contract, i.e. its substance and fundamental objective, as it is against this that it will be tested whether the data processing is necessary for its performance.”_

This leads me to split the processing into 2 linked processing purposes with respective sub-processing:

*→ Checking the authenticity/validity of the driving licence:*

* Manual check: Art 6(1)(c) (legal obligation to check).*
* Automated check: Art 6(1)(c) (depending on the technology used: legal obligation to check)
* Storage: Art 6(1)(f) (Legitimate interests): Proof that a check has been carried out) --> Here it is important to note that the notation of a check, the date and required data (vehicle class, period of validity) should be sufficient. **

*→ Verification (Is the person the person on the driving licence):*

* Manual check: Art 6(1)(c) (legal obligation to check).*
* Automated check: Art 9 (2) lit a (Explicit consent, assuming the presence of biometric data)
* Storage: depending on the category of data stored and the risk of litigation, possibly Art 9(2)(f) GDPR (closer examination required).**

_* Why not Abs 6 (1) lit. b GDPR: Example 6 of the Guidelines 2/2019 states that where an obligation to identify customers is provided for in national legislation, this identification constitutes a legal obligation and does not qualify as a measure necessary for the performance of the contract. Therefore, the legal basis is not Article 6(1)(b) but Article 6(1)(c)._
_** Why - in my opinion - does the verification of the driving licence fall under Art. 6 para. 1 lit. c DSGVO in connection with § 21 StVG, but the storage does not? Sec 21 VStG does not require any record keeping, but only the obligation to ensure that the driver has a valid driving licence before he starts driving (taking into account the general principles in Art 5, the legal norm is to be interpreted in conformity with European law in such a way that the least intrusive measure is  intended by the law)._ 
_Why can't the storage be based on Art 6 (1) lit b? I want to refer to example 6 of the Guidelines again. The EDPB otherwise also uses in the Guidelines the verbs "retain" or "store" in its examples, but it does explicitly use the formulation "requests to see their identity documents" in example 6 (identity verification). It must therefore be assumed that it is a deliberate reduction to "requests to see". This is also supported by the wording of the German and French language versions, which make a corresponding distinction in the examples (eg.: Einsicht in deren Ausweisdokumente (German), demande à voir leur pièce d’identité (French)_

*B. Is the storage of copies of driving licences appropriate and necessary for the fulfilment of the legal obligation according to Sec 21 StVG.*

Storage of copies of driving licences after they have been checked is not necessary for the fulfilment of the legal obligation and is also not expedient, as it represents a snapshot at the time of the check (it only serves as documentation that the legal obligation has been fulfilled and this proof can probably also be provided by milder means). The driving licence in Germany has no expiry date. Since the user can lose his driving licence for various reasons between initial registration and further use of the car sharing service, the storage is of no use.

I could not find more detailed information on the intervals at which the driving licence should be checked (new verification) → Maybe an outside counsel can provide more details_ {color}{color:#4c9aff}*_(not a data protection issue. My personal opinion: a verification before each start of the journey does not seem very user-friendly and also excessive, a one-time check in combination with clause 3.5. seems a little too lax)._*{color}

Car sharing and car rental companies handle copies of driving licences very differently. For the sake of completeness, I therefore refer to the following evaluation:

*Validation of driving licence*

*a. Type and scope of data processing*

In order to ensure that you, as our customer, have the necessary driving licence (validation of driving licence) to be able to use our service (vehicle sharing/vehicle rental), we carry out a validation of the driving licence before you use our service for the first time and at regular intervals thereafter. Only when this has been successful can you rent our vehicles. We are required to carry out a validation of the driving licence for legal reasons. For the purpose of the validation of the driving licence, photographs of your driving licence (front and back) and a current portrait picture (“selfie”) must be taken which are processed by us for the validation of the driving licence. The driving licence data is read out electronically from the pictures of the driving licence and checked for authenticity. In addition, a comparison is made between the portrait pictures (“selfie”) provided by you and the photo on your driving licence. In this process, so-called biometric data (personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person, which allow or confirm the unique identification of this natural person, such as facial images) of you within the meaning of Art. 9 (1) GDPR may also be processed.

The validation of the driving licence is partly carried out by our service provider Jumio (21 Worship Street, London, EC2A 2DW, United Kingdom) on our behalf and within the scope of data processing pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. The processing takes place in the United Kingdom and therefore outside the EU or the European Economic Area (EEA). However, the EU Commission has determined that an adequate level of protection comparable to the GDPR is guaranteed in the United Kingdom. Data transfers to the United Kingdom are therefore permissible pursuant to Art. 45 GDPR.

*b. Legal basis*

The processing of your personal data for the validation of the driving licence is necessary pursuant to Art. 6 (1) lit. c GDPR for the compliance with our legal obligation as we must determine that our customers are in possession of a valid driving licence pursuant Sec. 21 (1) No. 2 Road Traffic Act (“Straßenverkehrsgesetz”, StVG) in order to avoid criminal liability on the part of SHARE NOW as the keeper (“Fahrzeughalter”) of the vehicles.

Insofar as the photographs of your driving licence and your portrait pictures (“selfies”) and special categories of personal data pursuant to Art. 9 (1) GDPR are processed (biometric data), this is based on your consent, Art. 6 (1) lit. a in connection with Art. 9 (2) lit. a GDPR. Giving your consent is voluntary and you can withdraw it at any time with effect for the future. However, without the successful validation of your driving licence, you will not be able to use our service or carry out vehicle rentals with us.

*c. Retention period*

As soon as the processed data is no longer necessary for the outlined purposes, it will be deleted. In the case of our service provider Jumio, your data will already be deleted after 14 days. We generally store the data for the duration of the customer relationship. Even after termination of the contract, it may be necessary to store personal data from you in order to comply with contractual or legal obligations.

Unfortunately, with Leases it is quite common for the landlord to quite literally only supply the 4 walls of the building, infrastructure and conduits and nothing else such as: electricity, gas, water etc. I have had a look at this lease to see where the responsibility resides, and it seems in this agreement Bolt (as the Tenant) is responsible and will bare the costs for electricity, water, sewage, telecommunication and data and other services and utilities to or from the property, as per *Clause 11.1.*

Essentially, under this lease the landlord is obligated to provide service media whereas the Tenant (Bolt in this instance) is responsible to install the metres paying for services.

*Clause 11.1* states:

{color:#6554c0}*The tenant shall pay promptly all costs in connection with the supply and removal of electricity, gas, water, sewage, telecommunication and data and other services and utilities to or from the property*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}including any reasonable administrative charge made by the landlord for calculating such costs, where they are not billed by the relevant utility supplier directly to the landlord.

Hey Natali,

This “to be paid” sum does not refer to the monthly service usage. It is simply the aggregation of all balance activities by the end of the month. You can see this calculation within the box on the left hand side on this invoice. 

Briefly,

At the beginning of February, client’s balance was -1179.21£. During the month of February, they used 137.50£ worth of rides, so the balance went to -1316.71£. Then during the month, we received their payment for January (658£), so now the balance is -658.71£, which is what they need to pay - to turn their balance to 0£. 

So, as you can see while we reflect the monthly usage on the invoice (137.50£), the sum that needs to be paid is not really a use of service for a specific period (hence no specific invoice) but rather the calculation of what needs to be paid based on their balance activities (use of service, payments, balance from previous month etc.)

Hi Edi, apologies for keeping you waiting for the feedback. I have reviewed the contract:

* there are no clear grounds in the contract to claim the compensation of the implementation fee or replacement of the pickers in case we close the business/store. This is our business risk (sunk costs) - which we cannot expect the external provider to cover.
* however, based on section 5 - Warranties, Bolt has a right of the pickers' replacement in various cases, e.g. back performance, disciplinary offence or professionally inadequacy, experience or qualifications not met. Based on clause 5.2, 2 replacements are free of additional fee (3rd replacement in 6 month interval is subject to 12%commission) - therefore, we can claim that also free of at two implementation fees.
* the implementation fee represents the cost of recruitment and placement of TE. Then also, we should not pay for the pickers who were transferred from the closed stores to other stores, as the agency did not bear any new costs of recruitment.
* Finally - based on common sense and general civil law provisions, the agency was obliged to provide the services at professional level, supply qualified and reliable pickers, meeting the agreed requirements. If we do have the grounds to claim that the supplied pickers appeared to be inadequate for the work or badly performed, then we may argue that the services have been improperly performed, and therefore claim the compensation for the paid costs or mutually agree that the payments are not due. Of course, they can disagree - then we need to go to the court, but you may try to negotiate the settlement of the costs with them.

Conditions to define a bad order:

* Average courier speed >= 100 km/h
* Distance between courier and eater at the end of order >= 500 m
* Marketplace fee >= order price

Initial steps taken:

* implementing [GPS check |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4323803763/Weekly+courier+check+-+GPS+Fraud]for couriers within our weekly food fraud monitoring
* [rule|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/rules/edit/delivery_order_request/DELIVERY_GPS_FRAUD?tab=script] that blacklists destination addresses in UA, PL, PT

Query to identify GPS fraud orders based on input we have on _courier_on_order_delivered_check_ point; and to test them against our definition on a bad orders (MF>=user_price_eur):



{noformat}select 

etl.order_id,

etl.country_code,

date_trunc('week',etl.created_date) as weeks,

etl.user_price_eur,

oc.courier_id,

ROUND(ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate,2) AS courier_earnings_eur,

ROUND(CASE WHEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate>0 THEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END,2) AS marketplace_fee,

(CASE WHEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate>0 THEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END)*1.0/NULLIF(ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate,0) AS marketplace_fee_rate,

(CASE WHEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate>0 THEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END)*1.0/NULLIF(etl.user_price_eur,0) AS marketplace_fee_to_total_price_ratio,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.estimated_duration_from_provider_to_eater_s') as real) as estimated_time_from_p_to_e,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.actual_duration_from_provider_to_eater_s') as real) as actual_time_from_p_to_e,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.distance_from_provider_to_eater_m') as real) as distance_from_p_to_e_m,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.arrived_to_eater.lng') as real) as atc_lng,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.arrived_to_eater.lat') as real) as atc_lat,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.delivered.lng') as real) as del_lng,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.delivered.lat') as real) as del_lat,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lng') as real) as address_lng,

--cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lat') as real) as address_lat,

round(least((great_circle_distance(cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.delivered.lat') as double),cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.delivered.lng') as double),cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lat') as double), cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lng') as double))),((great_circle_distance(cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.arrived_to_eater.lat') as double),cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.courier_coords.arrived_to_eater.lng') as double),cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lat') as real), cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.delivery_address.lng') as double))))),3) as distance_between_eater_and_courier_at_the_end,

(cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.distance_from_provider_to_eater_m') as real)/1000)/(cast(json_extract_scalar(cod.input, '$.additional.delivery_data.order_info.actual_duration_from_provider_to_eater_s') as real)/3600) as speed_from_provider_to_eater,

(case when ((CASE WHEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate>0 THEN ce.earning_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate-o.delivery_price/etl.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END)*1.0/NULLIF(etl.user_price_eur,0)) >= 1 then 1 else 0 end) as mf_fraud

from 

ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders etl

LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS o ON o.id=etl.order_id AND o.city_id=etl.city_id  and o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)

LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_order_provider AS op ON op.order_id = o.id AND op.provider_id = o.provider_id and op.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)

LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_order_courier AS oc ON oc.order_provider_id = http://op.id  AND oc.state = 'delivered'  and oc.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)

--LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_courier_courier as cc ON cc.id=oc.courier_id

Hey [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] ,

Here I am sharing the answer that I received from our developers as to why this is happening (this seems to be a logic discrepancy):

_“that’s a classic issue we have with business resale rides provided by non-VAT-liable drivers._
_In short what’s happening there is:_

* _we receive a request to charge 8.9eur brutto_
* _we try to find out the net value of ride, which in case of non-vat-liable driver is still 8.9eur_
* _we need to apply VAT of reseller on top of net price -> we charge 10.77 eur (21% resale vat included)_

_The root of problem is that order service is not aware of specifics of business payment method and they just know the price which “invoice recipient” will pay._
_In resale model “invoice recipient” is reseller, so it indeed pays 8.9eur, but applies own VAT on top”_

-

Now, we have identified possible solutions to ensure such price discrepancy won’t happen, but these need to be discussed within the team and planned accordingly, so it might take time considering developers are rather packed. 

Could you perhaps enlighten me, what would be the risks if we fail to do this? When should we ideally fix it - is there a legal timeline we should stick to?

Hey! I put some comments in the doc.

In general, this is a good thing from GDPR perspective since it gives user more control and mitigates our risks for a possible data breach, if the data is made inaccurate on behalf Bolt employee. In such a case, we would be breaching the integrity of data. 

GPDR foresees that Bolt must apply suitable technical and organizational security measures to processing of data, so implementing such access rights, is also fulfilling such an obligation. Personal data should be accessed only if there is a legitimate purpose to do so, therefore if such employees do not really need to access admin and be able to make these changes, such access controls should be removed. We do not always need the consent of the person to alter data (as mentioned in the doc), there may be some cases where we need\may do it ourselves in order to be compliant (to make sure data in correct). 

One thing that caught my attention and could be discussed is the verification part. It is correct that we should ensure the user identity before altering, however a selfie verification maybe disproportionate to such purpose. Also , currently for CS assisted and HUB assisted changes, the security measures seem to be lower. 

If the product team is willing to implement such controls, let us know, so we could review the final process in detail also (wordings etc).

{quote}What exactly is it that your agents struggle with? Be as specific as you can as this will directly translate into the goals you’d expect from a particular training. We kindly ask you to attach a few ticket examples that would highlight problematic areas.{quote}

I won’t find ticket now, but agents tend to do mistakes when changing the city. Main reasons - incorrectly moves balance and creates new profile, even if there was a profile in that city already created (please see screenshot attached).

# If courier wants to go back to their OG city, we don’t create acc again, we block the one that won’t be used anymore and unblock the one that courier will work on.
# Balance must be moved or not moved based on these rules:

we *do not* transfer:
a) deposit (what it means: if courier had positive balance in city he wants to leave -> *we do not move the deposit (-25 Eur) to the new city if courier has positive balance*.) Cause we had cases when courier has let’s say 100 Eur balance in old city, wants to move to new city, thus he gets comp to old (+25 Eur) and deduction to new (-25) and he no longer continues to work with us. This way courier kind of gets his deposit back and get’s to keep the bag and no longer works with us)
b) a positive balance that is equal to 5 EUR or morewe *do* transfer:
a) any negative balance (For example, I work in Vilnius, I have -100 EUR, I want to work in Kaunas, you deduct 100 EUR in Kaunas, and the Vilnius account is compensated by the same 100 EUR. We do not ask courier to bank transfer their debt - we move the debt to the new city he’s going to work at)
b) positive balance, which is between 0.01 and 4.99 (because if there is less than 5 euros in balance, the courier will never get it, witch is absolutely unfair from courier perspective)

{quote}What would you like the training to achieve? → What specifically would your agents DO once they have completed the training?{quote}

# Agents would be able to copy the correct Balance values (based on rules mentioned above) - there would be 1 deduction and 1 compensation entry, no errors.
# Agents won’t create unnecessary profiles (if there’s already an old blocked profile in city that courier wants to switch to)

{quote}Why are your agents not doing this correctly at the moment? As I have mentioned before, the Courier wants to switch cities article contains a detailed procedure on how to switch cities in Admin. What exactly is it that is unclear about the process? Is there anything else that we need to take into consideration?{quote}

I’ll try to go step by step from KB and explain what might be confusing:
Negative balance: Ask them to settle this amount first - once the debt is clear, go to the next step <-  we don’t ask to settle the negative balance - we just move it to the active account.

* If the courier wants to switch cities back, block the new account and unblock the previous one  <- This step is being ignored and we have cases with several accounts in the same city (as in attached screenshot)

When changing the city, do not transfer the courier bag deposit to the new city <-  This has happened before- some agents transfered the deposit when courier had positive balance and courier no longer worked with us - thus got both his deposit and kept the bag.

{quote}And last but not least how does this impact your work?{quote}

This makes local COPS work a bit more difficult and couriers trust us a bit less if their balance is messed up while changing cities.

# If there are many accounts created for one partner, most of the time Balances will not be copied correctly - there will still be negative balance left in those old cities.
# Moreover, sometimes agents mix up accounts or do compensation/deduction multiple times - there was a case when freshly created account (after switching the city) had about 180 Eur debt. COPS team checked all the previous accounts and couldn’t explain why such debt accumulated. Thus we removed all the debt and allowed courier to start from 0 Eur in balance. Such tickets cost us both money and time.

Hi there Luane!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them a refund, therefore we are allowing them to financial gain and we are the ones who cause the fraud.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the user. 

On a different note, kindly be more precise in your escalations in the future and give as many details as possible about your case. Just links and a few words won’t do. Some examples to consider or think about: _What makes this case significant? How did you discover the matter? What is the current situation? What is suspicious in your opinion exactly? What have you already done? Who have you consulted on the matter? What is the expected outcome? What would you like us or propose to do? What is the impact of this issue on GMV and count? What is the urgency of the issue?_

Cheers,

Hi there!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them a refund, therefore we are allowing them to financial gain and we are the ones who cause the fraud.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the user.

On a different note, kindly be more precise in your escalations in the future and give as many details as possible about your case. Just links and a few words won’t do. Some examples to consider or think about: _What makes this case significant? How did you discover the matter? What is the current situation? What is suspicious in your opinion exactly? What have you already done? Who have you consulted on the matter? What is the expected outcome? What would you like us or propose to do? What is the impact of this issue on GMV and count? What is the urgency of the issue?_

Cheers,

*What is your request?* 
Kindly always provide context and information on why you have escalated a single user. The fraud team mainly focuses on bigger patterns of financial fraud and reviewing drivers single drivers without a cause is not a good use of our and your time. Now, without any comments, we do not have reason to suggest otherwise or an explanation on why this driver would have such flags other than he is fraudulent.

We will close this case and ticket, however, if you have important information to share that would change the driver’s case, feel free to submit a reply and we will consider it. Based on the current standing, the driver has caused more loss than gain and will not be reinstated.

Closing after having more in-depth discussion were the following has been concluded:

* using the [DeliveryShardLookup|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/common/delivery/router/async/DeliveryShardLookup.ts], class in the Bootstrap, will determine the generation of a service API, where the client still needs to specify the shard key. This is considered legacy and shouldn't be used for new endpoints
* in order to fully support RBS, where the client does not need to specify the shard key, we need to define a separate function to retrieve the {{city_id}} from the body in a separate class, other than {{DeliveryShardLookup}} and create a new {{Bootstrap}} class, which won't contain other routers that don't specify shard look up, nor uses {{DeliveryShardLookup}}.
* we should have different Bootstrap classes for different routing methods and not mix different routing methods in the same Bootstrap class.
* fully supporting RBS (using city_id from the request body) is a requirement for updating the sharding schema.
* all new endpoints should be defined in a new Bootstrap and configured to use [RBS|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3530555614/Guide+for+implementing+redirect-based+sharding].

Hello, we did not receive any documentation prior to blocking the driver's account. 

We checked the DVLA portal and found that the driver did not have the entitlement to drive, so we blocked the account. 

It's important to note that Bolt did not have any information about the driver's condition, and this was not a factor in the decision to block or unblock the account. Our sole consideration is whether the driver has a valid DVLA license.

The issue, in this case, is that the driver's license was not valid, yet he still took journeys on the Bolt platform, which made him non-compliant with our policies (he has completed 24 journeys whilst disqualified).

When drivers apply for account reactivation, we review their cases carefully. In this instance, we have reviewed the driver's case and decided not to reinstate his account. This decision was based on the fact that he had taken journeys on the Bolt platform without a valid DVLA license. If he had not taken any journeys, we would have considered reinstating his account. The reason for his DVLA disqualification by DVLA is not a factor in our decision-making process.



Reinstating his account would require us to deviate from our established processes.

further to the first (partial) analysis conducted by HL in December, please find enclosed here 

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Oorcg98xeIiLglRDCxAnVhvf6eEwECTrXts9-HEzF4s/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Oorcg98xeIiLglRDCxAnVhvf6eEwECTrXts9-HEzF4s/edit|smart-link]   an extensive memo prepared by MRA regarding the various ways to contest fines in Italy  and timeframes to make a claim.  Feel free to add your comments and questions directly in the doc, if something is still unclear. 

In addition to the already known remedies which are also mentioned on the fine minutes( ie claim filed with the Prefetto and Giudice di Pace) fines can be appealed in “autotutela”.



+*Autotutela*+ 

* The appeal must be submitted within +*60 days from the contestation of the violation or its notification*+ ( ie the date you received the fine minutes “verbale di notifica”). You can make a claim *only if the fine has not been paid yet*.
* The claim can be submitted by regular email sent the police or municipality asking the recipient to acknowledge receipt . However, *pec email is recommended* to keep track of the actual receipt. 
* The fine issuer is not obliged to rule on the appeal and may also  *remain silent.* In such an event the *fine is not cancelled.* 
* *The Autotutela doesn’t suspend/ freeze the time limit to appeal the fine before the Giudice di Pace/Prefetto*. You can accumulate Autotutela + appeal before GP/Prefetto.



+*Prefetto*+

* The appeal must be submitted within +*60 days from the contestation of the violation or its notification*+ ( ie the date you received the fine minutes “verbale di notifica”). You can make a claim *only if the fine has not been paid yet*.
* *If the appeal is rejected, a penalty equal to  twice the amount of the penalty imposed by the original fine applies.*
* Claim must be submitted *by pec* by filling in the ad hoc form and in any case including s*pecific details* re issuing authority, company, the fine report challenged, reason of the dispute. 
** *if the appeal has been submitted to the office of the issuing authority*, the Prefetto has to take a decision within *180 days from the submission of the appeal* (60 days for the transmission  of the documentation concerning the fine from the office of the issuing authority to the Prefect + 120 days for the  Prefect to decide)
** *if the appeal has been directly submitted to the Prefetto*, the Prefetto has to take a decision within  *210 days from the submission of the appeal*.
* The appellant may be requested for a *personal hearing.* 
* The whole proceeding form the moment the claim is made until the refusal decision of the Prefetto may last around 
+*330 days*+, in case of *submission to the office of the issuing authority of the fine*;
+*360 days*+, in case of *direct submission to the Prefetto +* any delay/ rescheduling in the event of personal hearings. 
* If the Prefetto dismisses our application/claim, the decision can be appealed before the Giudice di Pace within 30 days as of the dismissal notification. 



+*Giudice di Pace (alternatively*+ +to the appeal to the Prefetto)+ 

* The appeal must be submitted *within 30 days from the notification of the fine* ( ie the date you received the fine minutes “verbale di notifica”), or *60 days if the appellant does not reside in Italy*, and only if the fine has not been paid (and another appeal has not already been submitted to the prefect).
* +The assistance of a lawyer is not required+. However, if a lawyer is not appointed, +*the appellant must declare in the appeal act their residence or choice of domicile in the municipality where the Justice of the Peace is located*+.

* Claim must be submitted *by registered letter and must contain specific details (* see memo) 
* The Court will schedule the hearing for the appellant to appear. At the end of the hearing  the judge will read the ruling. The decision should be published +15 days later.+ 
* I refer you to the memo for more details about the *fees/ penalties to be paid in the event of dismissal* including counter party’s attorney fees. 
* The GP’s decision can be appeal  before the Court within 30 days as of the dismissal decision notification  or within 6 months as of the publication of the decision.



Please note that *impoundments fees* can only be challenged before the Giudice di Pace in the framework of the dispute of the main parking fine. However, it is not clear to me if we could make a claim in autotutela in addition to the GP to ask the cancellation of the impoundment fees.

*Please see summary below of the campaign:* 

See summary below a proposed giveaway campaign which we are aiming to roll out in the UK.

The giveaway’ aim is to incentivise drivers each month with a £500 bonus. A driver can be a Participant in this giveaway provided:

# The driver completes 100 trips (these are completed trips not cancelled).
# The driver maintains a score in the top 10% of UK drivers.
# Drivers must already be signed up to the Bolt platform or must sign up during the programme period.
# The driver must also satisfy the following eligibility requirements:

* Drivers must have a valid phone number and email address registered to their Bolt account.
* Drivers must comply with all relevant applicable laws in England and Wales.

Bolt can refuse participation into the giveaway if:

# A driver does not comply with these T&C’s and Bolt’s additional T&C’s.
# Any driver who has previously violated the T&C’s.
# Any driver who engages in fraudulent activity or gives rise to suspicion of fraudulent activity on the Bolt Platform.
# Any Driver whose conduct is contrary to the spirit or intent of the Program. 
# The prize draws are not open to Bolt employees and/or their families, or to any third party who is directly involved in administering the prize draw. 

When this criteria is met all eligible drivers are entered into a prize draw each month where 3 drivers are randomly selected and awarded £500. Three winners will be chosen for each monthly prize.

Can you please provide us with advice on the condition that the Driver must maintain a score in the top 10% of all UK drivers. We are conscious of reclassification issues, therefore want to ensure that before we launch this giveaway campaign that we are maintaining compliant and looking holistically at the campaigns we run. Please also let us know if you can identify any further Terms that may pose to be a problem under the reclassification matter.

Ideally we would prefer for the top 10% driver score criteria to stay because it’s a benchmark for recording drivers who perform “[good trips|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-gb/articles/10386276674962-I-have-issues-with-driver-score#:~:text=Driver%20score%20measures%20the%20percentage,outside%20of%20your%20set%20radius.]” and could realistically be eligible for top driver of the month based on their merits.

Hi there, again, Luane!

*Please take the time to read through our suggestions before escalating any further issues of the same nature.* 

The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them this satisfaction, therefore we are allowing them to financially gain. Asking for compensation is not fraud itself if you think about it. 

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes or encounter a higher surge of similar issues so these can be collected and then presented. It is up to you how to action the user.

Kindly be more precise in any of your escalations in the future and give as many details as possible about your case. Just links and a few words won’t do. Some examples to consider or think about: _What makes this case significant? How did you discover the matter? What is the current situation? What is suspicious in your opinion exactly? What have you already done? Who have you consulted on the matter? What is the expected outcome? What would you like us or propose to do? What is the impact of this issue on GMV and count? What is the urgency of the issue?_

Cheers,

Before someone goes on vacation, they should set up delegation in Workday under *My Delegations*. This ensures that all aspects of their work are covered in Workday. What delegation is: 

_Delegating a task is different from reassigning it. Reassignment permanently removes responsibility for a task from 1 user and assigns it to another. Delegation enables you to perform tasks on behalf of the original task owner for a period of time. Delegation doesn’t remove responsibility (ownership) for the task from the original task owner and, when the delegation period ends, any incomplete delegated tasks revert to the original owner._

In current version (GeoX 1.0) there are the following opportunities on the measurement:

* *TBR* (time-based regression):
1) In this case the clusters (aka GMAs predefined by Google based on *their* metrics) are randomised to test and control groups. Ads are launched only to test cluster.
2) control clusters are grouped to one counterfactual
3) this counterfactual is used as regressor for the test in a model

* *Matched* *markets*
Out of all the clusters, the best ones are chosen for the test market. And counterfactual is made only based on them

* *Trimmed match*
A city from test group is combined with some city from control group. And results are compared for each pair.


*NOTES:* 
1) Google knows that users travel from cluster to cluster and told on how they tackle it, but I think we ran out of time to discuss it (need to discuss further)

2) CMAs (aka clusters) are only shared case-by-case (so we cannot just ask for the definition of all clusters).

Essentially if you wanted to come out of this Lease before the end of 2023, Bolt would need to serve notice on {color:#bf2600}*Monday 1 May 2023*{color}*.*

(b)  Bolt remains in occupation of any part of the Property; 


(c)  there are any continuing subleases of the Property.

Hey [~accountid:615599b4bfa2c1006b7251c8], we should transfer payments only to the bank account of the driver, that is, payments cannot be sent to the bank of a third person. Such practice is already implemented in LV and is now being implemented in LT.

Please see the reasoning behind it:

* every transaction Bolt makes shall be substantiated by supportive documents - usually a contract between the parties. *Transfers to accounts of unrelated parties (relatives, friends) have no business rationale because Bolt has no contractual relations with such parties.* Such unjustified transactions will be spotted by (i) external auditors and/or (ii) tax authorities.
* transfers to unrelated parties *facilitate drivers' avoidance of legal responsibilities* (payment of loans, alimony, fines etc.). The most common claim is a payment of alimony. To enforce it, incomes transferred to the bank account of a driver are sized by a bailiff. If a driver's income is transferred to an unrelated account, it cannot be seized but can be withdrawn in cash avoiding payment of alimony. Due to this problem, Bolt receives a high number of bailiffs orders. Solution: the driver's income shall be transferred only to the driver's bank account. Further on, *please reject requests to transfer money to accounts of X person (relatives, friends).*
* transfers to unrelated parties allegedly contribute to tax avoidance. Money may be divided into smaller amounts and further transferred to other accounts locally or outside of EE. The more difficult it is to trace money transfers, the easier it is to avoid taxes.

After investigation and a lot of experimentation with moving the react-native sample project for android to the same gradle project as Chat SDK it was concluded the following:

* React Native tooling expect to have {{gradlew}} file inside of {{android}} project of the react native application.
* In gradle projects {{gradlew}} file must be in the root directory of the project on the same level as {{settings.gradle}} file.
* In Chat SDK {{settings.gradle}} and {{gradlew}} files lie in the directories hierarchy two levels above {{android}} directory which makes the react-native tooling work inconsistently.
* Making react-native app for android a part of the Chat SDK gradle project will make it a surrogate that may work less stable than having it in a separate gradle project with its own root {{build.gradle}}, {{settings.gradle}} and {{gradlew}}.

Keeping the react-native sample app in a separate gradle project makes all the developers working on it in a separate Android Studio window, the react native sample app for android can not use the same dependencies directory ({{libs.versions.toml}} file) as we use in the Chat SDK and it can not use the gradle build plugin from {{buildSrc}} directory. However keeping the build environment in a separate gradle project makes the project structure more familiar for react native developers, it is more straightforward and easier to debug.

So it was decided not to proceed with integrating react native sample app for android into the Chat SDK gradle project and keep the environment as it is.

There are two actual issues that we need to address. Please also write tests for it.

h2. Issue 1: upcoming stops are not taken into account for ETA calculation for cancellation fee

{{EtaCalculator.calculateForOrderCancellation}} does not include {{driver_active_order_stops}}. It means that:

* driver has an order A
* driver accepts the new b2b order B
* {{original_eta}} for order B is calculated to some value *taking into account* current driver’s order A and the upcoming stops for order A
* then, let’s say, driver got stuck in a traffic, so cancellation grace period is not applicable anymore ({{riderCancelsWithinGracePeriod}})
* rider for order B decides to cancel order B
* {{EtaCalculator.calculateForOrderCancellation}} is called
** actual behavior
*** {{driver_active_order_stops}} is an empty array
*** the check for {{actualEtaTooLong}} in {{CancellationFeeService.checkCancellationFee}} will return {{false}} because {{input.eta}} is calculated without taking actual upcoming stops into account, so {{input.eta}} will be less than {{input.original_eta}}
*** so, we are going to actually apply cancellation fee
** expected behavior
*** {{driver_active_order_stops}} includes upcoming stops for order A
*** {{input.eta}} now takes into account upcoming stops, and {{input.eta}} does not differ to much from {{input.original_eta}},
*** and {{actualEtaTooLong}} returns {{true}}, no cancellation fee applied

h2. Issue 2: original_eta is not updated after driver arrived to order A’s destination

* driver has an order A
* driver accepts the new b2b order B
* {{original_eta}} for order B is calculated to some value *taking into account* current driver’s order A and the upcoming stops for order A (say, it is 180 sec)
* then, let’s say, driver got stuck in a traffic, so cancellation grace period is not applicable anymore ({{riderCancelsWithinGracePeriod}})
* in opposite to “issue 1”, in this scenario driver did finish the order A, but it took some extra time (say, 2 minutes to go through the traffic)
* so, driver arrived to destination of order A and finished it
* now, rider for order B decides to cancel order B
* {{EtaCalculator.calculateForOrderCancellation}} is called
* {{driver_active_order_stops}} is an empty array (even after fix for issue 1) because there is no {{upcoming_steps}} for order A
** actual behavior
*** {{input.eta}} for {{CancellationFeeService.checkCancellationFee}} will be an ETA from current driver location to the pickup of order B
*** if it is smaller than {{input.original_eta}} by 20%, then, we are going to actually apply cancellation fee
** expected behavior (exact behavior is to be clarified*;* I ([~accountid:5db2cd1b0343b80c307a95c5]) see it this way)
*** if timestamp when client cancels order B > (order_try_creation_timestamp + original_eta)
**** then rider waited long enough, we did not fulfill our promise, therefore no cancellation fee applied
*** otherwise
**** rider has not yet waited until the end of the promised ETA, so we apply cancellation fee

* Impounded scooters → towing + deposit fees → can be challenged? * Impounded scooters → police fine not paid → if notified >60 days can be challenged? *Not challengeable as the deadline to appeal has expired. Usually fines include the instructions to pay online or at the post office.* 
* Impounded scooters → police fine not paid → if notified <60 days can be challenged? Yes/No with next steps and template and procedure to be followed to challenge. 
** *Fine notified less than 30 days → fine can be challenged before the Giudice di Pace and you can claim the refund of towing and deposit fees.*

** *Fine notified more than 30 days ago and less than 60 days ago → p*arking fine only (excluding towing+deposit fees) can be challenged via autotutela and Prefetto. See below procedure. 
** *Fine notified more than 60 days ago →* Fine cannot be challenged since the deadline expired. 



+*Legal grounds to challenge a fine*+

*As said above and in the MRA memo fines can appealed within 60 days at the latest  before Prefetto or autotutela or within 30 days only for GP  if you have valid legal grounds to contest the fines :* 

* *fine report incomplete or lacks formal requirement (* eg the inaccurate or missing data of the owner of the vehicle, the date (day, month, year), time or place of the infringement; the type and number of the vehicle; reference to the infringed rule and sanction applied; late notification >90 days as of the infringement) 
* *material errors* (eg different facts) 



+*Procedure*+ 

*Autotutela* : complete the template and send it via pec + attach relevant docs

*Prefetto*: complete the template and send it via pec + attach relevant docs

Attached is the *questionnaire* regarding the implementation of the *pass-through feature* completed and integrated by MRA yesterday after the first round of follow-up questions: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1keBHQlojhpo2YHs0z9aS8pewwTfIOU5s/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=105957310820692975090&rtpof=true&sd=true|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1keBHQlojhpo2YHs0z9aS8pewwTfIOU5s/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=105957310820692975090&rtpof=true&sd=true|smart-link] 

→ In a nutshell:

* Although  MRA's answer is not straightforward, I understand that in IT *the consent will not be required to pass fines costs on to the users.*
* *However,* users need to be *informed before the amount is charged* on their credit card (ie debit cannot be immediate) and *they should be able to dispute responsibility.*
* It seems that it would be possible to keep both options in upcoming T&Cs so that you can ask users to fully refund the fines costs by way of contractual rights OR enforce a contractual penalty for a fixed amount (amount TBD). FYI [@lachlan.craig|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03JV6YRREZ]
* *Administrative fees* covering our costs to handle each fine: based on 2022 decision of the ITA Consumer Authority, charging *30E o*n top of the fines costs might be too burdensome for users and the clause might be considered unfair. I’ve asked MRA to confirm whether 20E would be a safer amount vis à vis Consumer Authority.

*I’ve asked MRA to confirm the above (their email is not clear) as well as clarify what would be, in their opinion, a reasonable prior notice before debiting sums.*

* *Micro "penalties":*

Please note that  the *amount to be charged must correspond to the actual damage/losses suffered* by Bolt and Bolt should be able to evidence that this specific amount corresponds to the cost for internal check, 3PL pick up services etc…



*2/ REIMBURSEMENT OF PAST FINES*: art 5.8 of the current version of ITA T&Cs reads: _“You accept to pay  any fines, impound fees, penalties, and/or any other charges incurred by Bolt, that result from Your use of any E-Vehicle, You parking any E-Vehicle improperly (e.g. outside a Permitted Parking Area) or as a result of You violating any law, rule, regulation, or ordinance while using the Services.”_

If the clause is not unfair (therefore null and void) *we might be able to ask users to refund us for past fines. Pending MRA confirmation* in light of recent case law.

Hi there!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them this, therefore we are allowing them to financially gain. Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action a user as such. In this particular case, the user is already deleted and hence nothing further to do, really. 

On a different note, kindly be more precise in your escalations in the future and give as many details as possible about your case. Just links and a few words won’t do. Some examples to consider or think about: _What makes this case significant? How did you discover the matter? What is the current situation? What is suspicious in your opinion exactly? What have you already done? Who have you consulted on the matter? What is the expected outcome? What would you like us or propose to do? What is the impact of this issue on GMV and count? What is the urgency of the issue?_

Cheers,

Further to my slack message and for the benefit of those on this ticket: 

I appreciate in the past we may have disclosed data when requested (without challenging the request) but going forward we need to ensure that whenever we receive these requests we check:

* the identity of the requester (i.e. is it a legitimate request and do they have the authority to request/receive data)
* the legal ground/basis for their request
* whether the data is strictly necessary for their request/investigation
* whether we can limit the amount of data requested in any way (i.e. so that we only disclose what is strictly needed)

This is a requirement under privacy laws and the reason we need to do this is to show we have taken steps to assess the request and if we are ever challenged by a privacy regulator or the individual(s) the data belongs to as to why we disclosed their data, we can demonstrate we took appropriate steps before disclosing. My team (i.e. the Privacy Legal Team) is in the process of reviewing/updating the process and further guidance will be released in Q2 and shared with the business. * Wh support - For all year
* Maintenance costs - should be applied during the season. And off-season, only if there are maintenance, works to do.

April - December we are paying according to the expected workload. 
April-May 2000eur. (200h)
June-August 3500eur (400h)
September - December 2000eur (200h)
And for January - March 2000eur. (Potentially 200h, if the maintenance works are needed)

For Jan-March, maintenance costs apply only if it’s approved by us (Lead mechanic, Operations manager Maintenance) that there are maintenance works that are needed to be done. The payment for these months should be calculated by the man hours that are expected for repairs. 

Also, there should be an exit clause for the maintenance side, if Parnu 3pl can’t deal with the broken scooter count and we need to assist. This should give us the right to decrease the payment or cancel the maintenance payments if we need to take over. (if the broken scooter count is more than 20% for more than 1 month, this does not apply if scooters are waiting for parts)

* Compensation for extra repairs in Viljandi
Travel compensation 50eur. This includes = Fuel (186km) + car expenses.

Rescue trips should be done only if it’s approved by Lead mechanic or Operations Manager Maintenance.
It will happen only if the backlog is out of the norm.
That will depend on how many scooters are waiting for repair. And how complex is the repair. And what are the circumstances that broken scooter count is out of the norm. (more than 15% of the fleet)
If that is 3pl fault and lack of repairs made during the month. It’s their own responsibility to deal with scooters that need to be repaired. If that is caused by lacking spare parts. And 3pl needed to wait for spare parts. Then this is a legit reason for a rescue mission.

Mechanic day fee is related to rescue missions.
If the rescue mission is approved. Then this cost applies.

Rescue missions are capped. Maximum 15 rescue missions from July - August.

# No. A “credit statement” is not a legal document. It’s a document that “we are creating” for internal accounting purposes, but such a document should not trigger any further legal effects (although we can confirm my understanding with the legal team, if needed).

From a legal standpoint, the term “statement” has a very wide meaning, as it embraces any written representation, certification, affirmation, document, record, or accounting or bookkeeping entry made with respect to a claim or with respect to a contract, bid or proposal for a contract, grant, loan or other benefit from the Corporation.

In the case at hand, we decided to use “statements” to support the accounting entries and records that we will have to do in relation to the collection of an amount that falls out of the scope of VAT (i.e. city fines).

In line with the above, we can use the “credit statements” to support the accounting record of any amount that we may owe to a customer and the subsequent refund.

Both the “statements” and the “credit statements” will have an accounting purpose, but do not qualify as official documents for VAT purposes.

Irrespective of my answer to such a question, I would point out that we are using both the “statements” and the “credit statements” for internal purposes, so I guess that the users will not really care about the document itself. Hi there, 

Not only does fraud check if there were any updates to the route and destination, we also match these to the logical trip timeline and place based on the data. However, to point out your example then when a new destination is requested there runs a check that confirms if we can trust the user and allow this change or not. Further, as you have reported this change was rejected for a valid reason, but they continued on without approval. *This further stop (destination) should not have happened,* regardless of what the driver or rider has said, hence there is no point in us checking all or any user conversations.

Essentially, we’ve refunded because this ride wasn’t logged/approved in the App. The ride request had a really low prediction and there’s no destination change logged/approved in the App to justify the route the driver made. If the payment were successful, a refund wouldn’t happen from our side. If we collected the money, it would stay like that until the customer complained and CS would do a usual refund. 

*The main point is that please don’t compensate the driver this amount back in these cases.* The drivers must be educated that if the passenger requests a new destination, they must log that in the App and wait for approval. *If we don’t approve the change, they have to follow the message that is displayed to them in the App*. Check this KB article about it [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7643088163474|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7643088163474]

Hope we have clarified the reasons behind our procedures.

Hi there, Fred!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

We would also not hard action a user only based on their fraud graph/cards etc.

Additionally, the fraud team has set up some rules and restrictions that look at the user and calculate their risk. These rules also look at payment methods and relations and provide additional actions for the user to prove themself to be a good user. For example, we may challenge and send them through 3DS verification if we determine irregular activities. 

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them a refund, therefore we are allowing them to financially gain and we are the ones who cause the fraud.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the user.

Cheers,

Requirements:

REQ 1: Detected entrance should be shown to the eater in the checkout screen

REQ 2: All delivery location selection flows should be covered: previous order (i.e. delivery location), address selection via location-suggestions (new address, historical delivery address, historical ride address), tap on the “current location” screen. The only exception is:

REQ 3: If the eater moves the pin on the map in the checkout screen, we should not override coordinates (i.e. via the entrance detection model). The model should also not override the delivery location of any _subsequent_ orders having the delivery location manually adjusted by the eater.

REQ 4: Manual pin movements should be properly logged in Delta Lake so that they can serve as labels for offline model training.

REQ 5: Delivery system tables (e.g. order tables, delivery order history etc.) should always hold the actual eater-confirmed  delivery location (i.e. overridden coordinates if the model was used, original coordinates otherwise)

REQ 6: The system should always allow the choice to either serve the original coordinates or the overridden coordinates (if available) as instructed by {{targeting}} configuration. This also includes the scenario where an eater is at first on a “treatment” branch, but on a “control” branch later on (e.g. in an interleaved test).

REQ 7: ETAs and dispatching should be computed with respect to the _overridden_ coordinates, not the original coordinates.

REQ 8: The system should allow agents (CS, Map Prod, Engineers) to alter eater order locations that had incorrect predictions, in order to avoid propagating said incorrect locations to future orders.



NFREQ 1: The solution should be backwards-compatible with eater app versions i.e. we don’t want to do any eater app code changes, nor do we want to wait for new version adoption

*Estonian labour law* 

*1. Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* Yes

*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?* No

*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* In a dispute over the nature of the contract (if the contract has the characteristics of both an employment and another contract), the parties are deemed to have an employment relationship unless the employer proves otherwise.

*4. Are RSAs expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* The main characteristic of the employment contract is the submission to the employer’s management and control. The greater the control over a person (contractor), the more likely he/she is considered an employee. To refute the employment presumption set forth in § 1 (2) of the Employment Contracts Act, the alleged employer must prove above all that the employee was not subject to its management and control and was largely independent in choosing the way, time and place of doing the work.

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* Yes, up to 3 years

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators?* Drivers or group action. But once the Directive is adopted, and after it is transported into the
local law, it will become very likely that Labour or Tax authorities would use its _ex-officio_ right to launch investigations into related subjects. The Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work (if the 2/3 out 5 criteria are met).  Member States will be required to establish a framework for effective implementation of the legal presumption through
appropriate measures, it will also mean strengthening controls and field inspections.

*7. Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* No

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?* Employment matters are state fee free and access to employment litigation is well established.

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?* No. Court rulings have legal effect only for the parties of the dispute. So no court ruling on reclassification would be automatically applicable to all the drivers. But the effect of a court precedent may trigger similar court actions.
